title: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
gist: Scott Wiener, newly elected to Nancy Pelosi's San Francisco House seat, plans to push strong federal AI regulation, citing a METR report read as evidence of Anthropic recursive self-improvement. He opposes broad federal preemption of state AI laws and is only cautiously optimistic given Congress's record and Trump's stance.

insights.claim: Scott Wiener, author of California's SB 1047 and SB 53, won the open San Francisco House seat vacated by Nancy Pelosi and could play a key role in setting federal AI policy.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: A frontier-AI-safety legislator now sits in Congress, raising odds of federal AI rules.

insights.claim: Wiener wants a strong, empowered, nimble federal AI regulator, noting Rep. Ro Khanna has proposed legislation to create one.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: Points to a possible new federal AI agency as a policy option.

insights.claim: Wiener's priority list includes whistleblower protections, testing and auditing requirements, a kill switch requirement, and aggressive congressional oversight of AI labs.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: Indicates likely compliance burdens for frontier labs under future federal legislation.

insights.claim: Wiener opposes broad federal preemption of state AI laws, even though some proposed federal bills would require it, arguing states are laboratories that stay nimble where Congress is not.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: Preemption fight is a key variable for whether state AI laws survive.
insights.quote: States are, as Brandeis says, laboratories

insights.claim: Wiener would like to serve on a congressional select committee on AI, which Democrats have discussed since September.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: A select committee would be a venue for AI oversight hearings.

insights.claim: SB 1047 would have been the first real frontier AI legislation in the US but was vetoed by Gavin Newsom; the lighter-touch SB 53 was signed, and both have inspired proposed federal legislation.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: State bills are templates for the federal framework.

insights.claim: Wiener read a METR report released the prior day as widely interpreted evidence that Anthropic has achieved recursive self-improvement, and cited it as proof that time to regulate is running out.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: Recursive self-improvement narratives are now driving policy urgency; note the report is characterized as widely interpreted, not confirmed.

insights.claim: Wiener argues AI is moving so fast that society could sleepwalk into disaster and says we need to slow it down.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: A lawmaker openly favoring slowdown signals a more restrictive policy tail risk.
insights.quote: We need to slow this down

insights.claim: Wiener says loss of control over AI is a very dangerous risk and that once recursive self-improvement is reached it is potentially a recipe for total loss of control.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: Safety-movement language is entering mainstream legislative discourse.

insights.claim: Wiener had hoped Congress would act decisively on AI before the end of the year but says that does not appear to be happening.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: Near-term federal AI legislation is unlikely.

insights.claim: Wiener's campaign received over $3 million from Public First Action, a pro-AI-regulation nonprofit substantially funded by Anthropic, drawing attacks that he is too close to the AI industry.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Anthropic is financing political support for AI regulation.

insights.claim: Wiener calls the attacks over Public First's support shockingly cynical, saying he regulated AI over Big Tech's objection.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: Shows AI-industry money cuts both ways in campaigns.

insights.claim: There is a large gap between Wiener's Bay Area, AGI-pilled perspective and a national AI mood anchored by opposition to data centers.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Safety-focused regulators and the public are worried about different things.

insights.claim: Voters approved 40 out of 41 anti-data-center ballot measures on Tuesday, but Wiener sees the revolt as tied to local concerns like electric bills, water use and impacts near homes rather than AI risk.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: Data center opposition is not the same constituency as AI-safety support.

insights.claim: Wiener describes himself as only cautiously optimistic about Congress reining in AI given its poor record of regulating tech.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
insights.so_what: Base rate for passage is low.

insights.claim: President Trump called catastrophic AI risk a hoax in September and has shown unwillingness to collaborate with China, which Wiener sees as essential to preventing the worst consequences of AI.
insights.speaker: Grace Huckins
insights.so_what: Executive-branch hostility is the main barrier to federal AI safety rules and US-China coordination.

insights.claim: Wiener hopes it does not take a disaster to spur the president to act, but if so that it is as small as possible.
insights.speaker: Scott Wiener
